column1: # Data sources axis: REFERENT -- MULTI-VALUED.
# Principle of division: WHAT, OUTSIDE THE SIGNAL, COULD SHOW ITS VALUES TO BE
# WRONG. NOT how the values were produced (that is `provenance`), not what they
# depict (`domains`), not how they are obtained (`access`).
# Derived 2026-10-08 by three independent runs (SYNTHESIS.md section 7). All
# three reached this principle in different words and all three produced three
# values plus a miss-recorder, agreeing on `stipulated` by name and on the top
# split -- answerable to the world, or not. They DIVERGED on where the second
# cut goes, and each run's unplaceable case turned out to be the cell another
# run's cut separated: D1 and D3 subdivided the empirical side, D2 the
# non-empirical side. The owner adopted the UNION of their three doubts, so
# `formal` is attested by D2 and by the cases D1 and D3 could not place --
# D1 derived a fourth value and killed it from both ends, D3 called its
# formal-mathematics corpus "the recursion trap I could not dissolve".
# MULTI-VALUED (D1, D3; D2 single-valued and scoped by fiat to one channel). A
# unit-test suite over real code is `particular` in its code and `formal` in its
# pass/fail, and both hold.
# NO SCOPE PREDICATE and it applies to EVERY source, not only computed ones --
# all three runs, independently. D1's reason: a predicate would make this axis a
# function of a multi-valued `provenance`, so a hybrid source would be in and
# out of scope at once.
# ON THE ENTITY, like `provenance` -- but UNRESOLVED, see the notes on
# `stipulated`: all three runs found one engine spanning several values by task.
# `unknown` is a CODING STATE. D1 argues an EMPTY set is a coding ERROR here,
# unlike on `provenance`, since every signal is answerable to something or
# declares that it is not; recorded as one run's claim, not as a rule.
node_id
particular
column4: the values report specific individuals that existed independently of this source
column5: you can name the individual each item is about, and an error in it is an error ABOUT that individual
column6: fails when no individual is nameable even in principle, only a population or a law (generic); fails when nothing outside the specification is being reported
column7: SDSS and LSST imaging of actual objects; fastMRI scans and MIMIC records of actual patients; Wikipedia and Project Gutenberg texts; The Stack's actual repositories; GTSRB's actual street signs
column8: D1 `real-particular`, D3 `particular`, and inside D2's `empirical`. The name deliberately says nothing about the KIND of individual -- a galaxy, a patient and a traffic sign are all particulars, and which one it is belongs to `domains`

column1: generic
column4: no individual is reported, but part of the specification was fixed by measurement or fitting, so "this is unrealistic" is a complaint owed an answer
column5: a domain expert can argue the source is a poor approximation and the argument has a subject matter; some constant in it traces back to an observation
column6: fails when nobody claims the source approximates anything real, so "unrealistic" has no purchase (stipulated); fails when specific individuals are reported (particular)
column7: CMIP6 climate runs; OC20 and ANI-1x DFT energies; the UVA/Padova type-1 diabetes simulator; PDEBench solver outputs; SERGIO gene-network simulations
column8: D1 `real-general`, D3 `generic`; D2 declined this cut and handed it to a queued axis. THIS IS THE CELL THE SPLIT WAS BUILT FOR: the diabetes simulator is `generic` and a locomotion task in the same class of engine is `stipulated`, which is the distinction one value could not hold. D3's open case: PDE benchmarks read `generic` by specification and `stipulated` by falsifiability

column1: formal
column4: the values answer to an abstract system whose facts EXCEED its specification; a disagreement is settled by computation or proof, never by observation
column5: the rules are stated in full and yet a value in the data is something that had to be found -- searched for, solved or proved -- rather than chosen
column6: fails when the specification settles every value directly, so there is nothing to find (stipulated); fails when an observation could settle it (particular, generic)
column7: terminal outcomes from the rules of Go and chess; Lean and Coq proof checking; satisfiability of generated k-SAT instances; unit-test pass/fail over real code
column8: D2's value, and the one the owner's union restores. D1 derived it as `self-constituting`, then killed it -- "Wikipedia fell to real-particular, authored puzzles to stipulated, nothing left between" -- and D3 met it as its undissolvable recursion trap. That two runs reached the cell and could not keep it, while the third kept it with a working test, is why it is here. FLAGGED: never placed against real names. Its boundary with `stipulated` is the one this axis has not tested

column1: stipulated
column4: the generating specification IS the standard; no amount of looking at the world, and no computation, could show an item wrong
column5: the source cannot be in error, only badly chosen; there is no verification step definable over its items
column6: fails if some fact about the data had to be discovered rather than declared (formal); fails if anyone is entitled to call it unrealistic (generic)
column7: dSprites and Shapes3D factor grids; Erdos-Renyi and stochastic-block-model draws; BBOB analytic test functions; MuJoCo locomotion morphologies; Procgen and MiniGrid levels; Atari frames as rendered
column8: Same name and same characteristic in all three runs -- the strongest single agreement on this axis. GRANULARITY IS UNRESOLVED HERE, and all three runs found it: one physics engine spans several values depending on the task modelled (D3), Habitat's scan-then-render case relocates rather than dissolves (D1), and D2 found the value USE-DETERMINED for an engine named as the source -- which contradicts attaching this axis to the entity. See SYNTHESIS.md section 7

column1: referent-other
column4: the values answer to something none of the above describes
column5: a reviewer can say what would show the values wrong and why no value above fits
column6: not the case where the paper does not say -- that is the `unknown` coding state
column7: none named on purpose; D3's unplaceable candidates were normative standards and counterfactual scenarios; D2 considered and declined a `conventional` fourth value
column8: the answerable/stipulated split is intended to be exhaustive, so this is expected to stay near-empty. Kept so an ontological miss is recorded as a miss
